$comment: char VALUE codegen across all targets (D-CSUBSET-CHAR-STRING-VALUE-CODEGEN + D-CSUBSET-CHAR-INT-WIDENING + D-CSUBSET-BARE-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-TARGET): byte load (movzx/LDURB), byte store (mov r/m8/STURB, baseline pipeline), the char->int promotion, int->char Trunc. `neg=(char)200` then `isneg = neg<0` makes the exit code a per-target signedness WITNESS: bare `char` is SIGNED on x86_64/pe64 (SExt/movsx -> -56<0==1 -> 65+66+1=132), and DSS CURRENTLY RESOLVES BOTH arm64 ROWS AS UNSIGNED (ZExt/uxtb -> 200<0==0 -> 65+66+0=131). ⚠ ABI CORRECTION — an earlier revision of this comment asserted that bare `char` is UNSIGNED on arm64 `per the AArch64 ABI`, as though signedness were a property of the ARCHITECTURE. THAT IS FALSE, and it is exactly what let the arm64:macho64 row below be written as if it asserted correct behaviour. What is actually true: AAPCS64 leaves bare-`char` signedness IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED; the AArch64/GNU-Linux platform ABI chose UNSIGNED, Apple's arm64 platform ABI DIVERGED and chose SIGNED, and clang follows the PLATFORM rather than the architecture. Signedness is therefore an (architecture × PLATFORM) property, not an architecture property. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64 with Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101): (a) `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target aarch64-linux-gnu` defines __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1, while `-target arm64-apple-darwin` does NOT define it at all (nor do x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu or x86_64-pc-windows-msvc); (b) `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` compiles clean (rc 0) for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and FAILS (rc 1) for aarch64-linux-gnu; (c) THIS example's exact expression `65 + 66 + ((char)200 < 0)` constant-evaluates to 132 for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and to 131 for aarch64-linux-gnu (clang note: `expression evaluates to '131 == 132'`); (d) on THIS main.c clang emits `ldrsb` (sign-extend) for the char locals on native arm64-darwin and `ldrb` (zero-extend) under --target=aarch64-linux-gnu. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROWS BELOW: the two x86_64 rows (132, inherited from the top-level exitCode) and the arm64:elf64 row (131) are CORRECT and assert real behaviour. The arm64:macho64 row is NOT — it pins a known DSS defect and carries its own $comment saying so. Read that row's $comment before touching this example.
